description: Categorize the transactions with no category — **many merchants in one call**. Send every merchant-to-category decision you have worked out as one `assignments` list rather than calling this once per merchant. **Dry-runs by default**: it returns what the whole batch would change and writes nothing until you call it again with commit true, so show the user the table and let them answer once. Rows categorized by hand are never touched, rows assigned by a rule are left to the rule, and every row it does change is marked AI so the batch stays findable. The document is copied to a timestamped .bak before anything is written. A row covered by two assignments refuses the batch rather than picking one.

assignments.description: One entry per category-and-scope. Up to 200 in a call.

category_id.description: The category to assign. Ids come from `category_tree`.

from.description: Narrow to charges on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

merchant.description: The normalized merchant name, exactly as `uncategorized_merchants` printed it. Covers every row of that name within the dates and account given.

to.description: Narrow to charges on or before this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

transaction_ids.description: Specific transactions, instead of a merchant. Not both.

commit.description: Default false. False previews the whole batch and writes nothing; true makes it.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

name: assign_category
title: Assign categories to transactions
